name: ZITLAS Chikoo Curd Bowl
description: Fresh chikoo (sapota) mashed into curd — introducing a fruit widely grown in Maharashtra's Dahanu region, not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Mash the chikoo.
Fold into curd along with cardamom powder.
Eat immediately, chilled.
why_it_works: Chikoo is a genuinely new fruit for the database, widely grown around Dahanu in Maharashtra's Palghar district
Naturally sweet, needs no added sugar
Entirely no-cook

name: ZITLAS Amla Chutney Toast
description: A tangy Indian gooseberry (amla) chutney spread on toast — introducing a fruit not used anywhere else in the database, prized in Maharashtrian home remedies.
instructions: Blend amla with jaggery and a little green chilli into a tangy chutney.
Toast the bread.
Spread the amla chutney generously over the toast.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Amla is a genuinely new, notably vitamin-C-rich fruit for the database, widely used in Maharashtrian home remedies
Very tart flavour balanced by jaggery
No-cook chutney, quick to make

name: ZITLAS Kulith Pithi Bhakri
description: A bhakri made from horse gram (kulith) flour — a Maharashtra-specific everyday use of horse gram, distinct from the North Indian usal preparation of the same legume already in the database.
instructions: Mix kulith flour with onion, cumin seeds, green chilli and enough warm water to form a soft dough.
Pat directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa into a thin round.
Cook covered until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Using kulith as a flour for bhakri is a genuinely different Maharashtrian everyday technique from the sprouted, boiled usal preparation already in the database
Horse gram is notably higher in iron than most other legumes used in the database
Traditionally considered warming, popular in Western Maharashtra winter cooking

name: ZITLAS Gavar Bhaji with Bhakri
description: Cluster beans (gavar) cooked into a simple sabzi and served with bhakri — introducing a vegetable not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Knead jowar flour into a bhakri and cook on a tawa.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric, add chopped gavar and a little water.
Cover and cook 12-15 minutes until tender.
Stir in crushed peanuts.
Serve hot with the bhakri.
why_it_works: Cluster beans are a genuinely new vegetable for the database, with a distinct slightly bitter, fibrous character
Peanuts add protein and crunch
Everyday Maharashtrian home vegetable rarely represented in fitness recipe collections

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Shev Bhaji Breakfast Bowl
description: Thin gram-flour sev simmered in a fiery Khandesh-style gravy — an iconic dish from Maharashtra's Khandesh (Northern Maharashtra) region, distinctly spicier than any other breakfast gravy already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add kala masala.
Add water to form a gravy and simmer 10 minutes.
Just before serving, add the sev to the hot gravy so it softens slightly but keeps some bite (it will turn mushy if added too early).
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Khandesh's distinctive fiery kala masala is a genuinely different spice blend from the goda masala, Kolhapuri or Malvani masalas already used across the database
Sev-in-gravy technique is a genuinely different construction from any other breakfast dish already in the database
Northern Maharashtra regional identity, distinct from Kolhapur, Konkan or Vidarbha

name: ZITLAS Ukad Rice Dumpling Bowl
description: Soft, unshaped rice-flour dumplings simmered directly in a mild curry — a distinct steamed-then-simmered technique from the pleated modak or steamed idli formats already in the database.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth dough, then shape into small irregular dumplings by hand (no pleating or precise shaping needed).
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric, saute onion until soft.
Add water to form a thin gravy, bring to a simmer, then drop in the raw dumplings and cook 8-10 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Cooking rough, unshaped dumplings directly in a simmering gravy (rather than steaming pleated ones separately) is a genuinely different technique from the modak already in the database
Simple, rustic home-style preparation
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Ber Chutney Toast
description: A sweet-tart jujube (ber) chutney spread on toast — introducing a fruit not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Simmer deseeded ber with a splash of water and jaggery for 4-5 minutes until softened.
Mash into a chunky chutney and stir in roasted cumin powder.
Toast the bread.
Spread the ber chutney over the toast.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Ber is a genuinely new fruit for the database, commonly found growing wild across rural Maharashtra
Distinct sweet-tart flavour from any other fruit chutney already used
Quick, minimal cooking

name: ZITLAS Fansachi Bhaji Bowl
description: Jackfruit seeds cooked into a spiced sabzi — a distinct part of the jackfruit plant from the raw jackfruit flesh (phanas bhaji) already in the database, with a starchier, nuttier character.
ingredients: Jackfruit seeds, boiled and halved — 100 g
instructions: Boil the jackfruit seeds until soft, then peel and halve them.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add the boiled seeds with a little water, simmering 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with bhakri.
why_it_works: Jackfruit seeds are a genuinely distinct part of the plant from the flesh already used in the database, with notably more protein and a starchier, chestnut-like texture
A traditional food-waste-reduction ingredient, using a part of the fruit often discarded
Different regional vegetable altogether from any tuber or gourd already in the database

name: ZITLAS Sandge Bhaji Breakfast Bowl
description: Sun-dried lentil-paste dumpling pieces (sandge), rehydrated and cooked into a light curry — a traditional Maharashtrian pantry-preservation ingredient distinct from the wadi already used in this collection.
ingredients: Dried sandge, soaked and broken — 50 g
instructions: Soak the dried sandge in warm water for 10 minutes until slightly softened, then break into pieces.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add the sandge pieces and a little water, simmering 8-10 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with bhakri.
why_it_works: Sandge (sun-dried lentil-paste pieces, distinct in shape and drying method from the dumpling-style wadi already used) represents another traditional Maharashtrian food-preservation technique
Concentrated protein from the dense, dried lentil paste
Genuinely different texture from a fresh-dal curry

name: ZITLAS Roasted Kardai Seed Chutney Toast
description: A chutney made from roasted safflower (kardai) seeds — Solapur's traditional oilseed, spread on toast, introducing a seed not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Dry-roast the safflower seeds until fragrant, about 3-4 minutes.
Grind with garlic, red chilli and a little water into a thick chutney.
Toast the bread and spread the chutney generously.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Kardai (safflower) seeds are a traditional Solapur-region oilseed genuinely not used anywhere else in the database, offering a distinct nutty, slightly bitter flavour and real protein
Represents Solapur's specific agricultural identity beyond the peanut chutney already covered
Quick, no-cook once the seeds are roasted

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Wangi Bharit with Kala Masala
description: Roasted eggplant mash seasoned with Khandesh's distinctive kala masala — a genuinely different spice profile from the plain, Vidarbha-style or garlic-tomato bhardas of eggplant already in the database.
instructions: Roast the eggplant directly over a flame until charred and soft.
Peel and mash the flesh.
Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add kala masala, then stir in the mashed eggplant.
Serve hot with jowar bhakri or rice.
why_it_works: Kala masala's distinctive dark, intensely roasted spice blend is genuinely different from the goda masala or Vidarbha spicing already used for eggplant dishes in the database
Represents Khandesh's specific culinary identity, distinct from every other Maharashtra region already covered
Smoky, bold flavour

name: ZITLAS Vali Dana Usal Bowl
description: Fresh green val beans (not the dried version used elsewhere) cooked usal-style — a genuinely different texture and seasonal ingredient from the dried Val (Lilva Beans) Usal Bowl already in the database.
ingredients: Fresh green val beans (vali dana) — 120 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add fresh val beans and a little water, simmering 12-15 minutes until tender (fresh beans cook faster and stay greener than the dried version).
Serve hot with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Using the fresh, in-season green bean rather than the dried version already used in the database gives a genuinely different texture — plumper, greener, quicker-cooking
Seasonal winter specialty distinct from the year-round dried pulse
Same legume, meaningfully different form and cooking behaviour

name: ZITLAS Kakadi Chi Koshimbir Bowl
description: A Maharashtrian-style cucumber-peanut koshimbir salad — a distinct salad tradition and format from a generic raita or Western-style salad already in the database.
instructions: Grate the cucumber and lightly squeeze out excess water.
Mix in crushed roasted peanuts, chopped green chilli and coriander.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve immediately as a side or light lunch component.
why_it_works: Koshimbir is a specific Maharashtrian salad tradition with its own peanut-forward, minimally-dressed technique, distinct from a curd-based raita or an oil-vinegar Western salad
Very low calorie, high protein from peanuts relative to the volume
Traditional accompaniment reframed as a light standalone lunch component

name: ZITLAS Gavar Usal Bowl
description: Cluster beans cooked usal-style with sprouted moong — a distinct vegetable-legume combination from any other usal already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add chopped gavar and moong sprouts with a little water, simmering 12-15 minutes until the beans are tender.
Serve hot with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Combining a vegetable (cluster beans) with a legume (moong sprouts) in one usal is a genuinely different composition from any single-legume usal already in the database
Higher fiber and protein together than a vegetable-only sabzi
Genuine vegetable diversity in the usal family

name: ZITLAS Custard Apple and Paneer Bowl
description: Fresh custard apple (sitaphal) pulp tossed with paneer cubes — celebrating Marathwada's Beed district, famous for sitaphal cultivation, in an unusual sweet-savoury pairing.
instructions: Carefully deseed the custard apple and separate the pulp.
Toss with cubed paneer and a little black pepper.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: Custard apple is a genuinely new fruit for the database, specifically celebrating Marathwada's Beed district which is one of India's largest sitaphal-growing regions
Unusual but genuinely different sweet-savoury pairing from the mango-paneer or watermelon-paneer combinations already used
Seasonal, regional specialty

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Patodi Curry
description: A besan dough rolled into a log, sliced into rounds, and simmered in a spiced curry — a genuinely different construction from the steamed, diamond-cut Patodi already in the database.
instructions: Cook besan with water and curd on low heat, stirring continuously, until it thickens into a very stiff dough.
While still warm, roll into a log shape and let cool completely, then slice into rounds.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add kala masala and water to form a curry.
Gently add the patodi rounds and simmer 5-6 minutes to absorb the flavour.
Serve hot with rice or roti.
why_it_works: Rolling into a log and slicing into curry is a genuinely different construction technique from the steamed, tin-poured, diamond-cut Patodi already in the database
Khandesh's kala masala gives a distinctly different flavour direction from the Gujarati-adjacent Maharashtrian patodi already used
Curry format rather than a dry steamed snack

name: ZITLAS Kohla Bhaji Bowl
description: Ash gourd (kohला/petha vegetable) cooked into a light, mild sabzi — introducing a very high-water-content vegetable not used anywhere else in the database.
ingredients: Ash gourd, peeled and cubed — 150 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric, saute onion briefly.
Add cubed ash gourd, cover and cook 10-12 minutes until soft (it releases plenty of its own moisture).
Serve with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Ash gourd is a genuinely new vegetable for the database, with an even higher water content and milder flavour than ridge gourd or bottle gourd already used
Very low calorie, gentle on digestion
Simple, minimal-spice preparation

name: ZITLAS Amla Achaar Rice Bowl
description: Warm rice tossed with a spiced amla pickle-style mix — a distinct tangy rice preparation using a pickle-inspired technique, not resembling any curry-topped rice already in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, turmeric, red chilli powder — 6 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, turmeric and red chilli powder (a pickle-style tempering).
Add chopped amla and cook 4-5 minutes until slightly softened but still tangy.
Toss the amla mixture through warm rice.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Pickle-style tempering technique applied directly to rice (rather than making a separate pickle to eat alongside) is a genuinely different concept from any curry-and-rice dish already in the database
Amla's tartness and vitamin C content in a warm, everyday format rather than a preserved pickle
Quick, distinctive flavour

name: ZITLAS Kurdai Bhaji Bowl
description: Sun-dried rice-and-lentil paste snack pieces (kurdai), rehydrated and cooked into a curry — a distinct dried-and-stored Maharashtrian ingredient from the wadi or sandge already used in this collection.
ingredients: Dried kurdai, soaked and broken — 50 g
instructions: Soak the dried kurdai in warm water for 10 minutes, then break into pieces.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add the kurdai pieces with a little water, simmering 8-10 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with bhakri.
why_it_works: Kurdai (rice-and-lentil based, distinct from the pure-lentil wadi or sandge already used) is a third genuinely different traditional Maharashtrian dried-food-preservation ingredient represented in this collection
Different base composition (rice plus lentil, rather than pure lentil) from wadi or sandge
Traditional pantry-staple technique

name: ZITLAS Vidarbha Zunka Powder Rice Bowl
description: Dry-roasted besan powder (rather than cooked wet zunka) mixed directly into warm rice with oil — a genuinely different construction from the standard cooked Zunka Bhakri Bowl already in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, red chilli powder, garlic — 5 g
instructions: Dry-roast the besan in a pan until fragrant and slightly darker in colour, then cool and set aside as a powder.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, garlic and red chilli powder.
Toss the roasted besan powder and the tempered oil through warm rice until evenly coated.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Using dry-roasted besan powder mixed directly into rice — rather than cooking it into a wet zunka first — is a genuinely different construction from the standard Zunka Bhakri Bowl already in the database
Vidarbha home-style rice preparation, quick and rustic
Different textural experience — grainy and dry-coated, not saucy

name: ZITLAS Leftover Varan Rice Fritters
description: Leftover varan (plain dal) and rice mashed with besan and baked into fritters — a distinct leftover-rescue technique using plain varan specifically, different from the spiced amti-based Leftover Amti Rice Cutlets already in the database.
instructions: Mash leftover varan and rice together with besan, cumin seeds and green chilli until it holds together.
Shape into small patties.
Arrange on a lightly oiled tray and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Uses plain, unspiced leftover varan specifically, distinct from the spiced leftover amti already rescued in another recipe in the database
Baked rather than pan-fried, keeping this meaningfully lighter

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Chicken Rassa
description: Chicken cooked in Khandesh's famously fiery kala masala — a distinct regional spice identity from the Kolhapuri, Malvani or Vidarbha saoji chicken curries already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until deep golden, add garlic and kala masala.
Add the chicken and water, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with bhakri, deliberately very spicy in the Khandesh tradition.
why_it_works: Khandesh's kala masala is a fourth genuinely distinct regional chicken curry identity in the database, alongside Kolhapur, Malvani and Vidarbha
Northern Maharashtra is famous for producing some of the spiciest food in the state
Deep, dark, intensely roasted spice character distinct from the others

name: ZITLAS Fish Amchur Konkan Bowl
description: Fish cooked with dried mango powder (amchur) as the souring agent instead of kokum or tamarind — a distinct technique from every other Konkan fish preparation already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add amchur and turmeric.
Add water to form a light gravy, bring to a simmer, then gently add the fish and cook 6-8 minutes until just cooked through.
Serve with rice.
why_it_works: Amchur as the souring agent gives a genuinely different tang from the kokum used in every Konkan or Malvani fish dish already in the database
Distinct dry-sour flavour direction rather than the fruity tartness of kokum or tamarind
Lighter, simpler preparation

name: ZITLAS Egg Khandeshi Curry Bowl
description: Boiled eggs simmered in Khandesh's kala masala — a distinct regional egg curry identity from the Kolhapuri, Bengali panch-phoron or Vidarbha saoji egg curries already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until deep golden, add garlic and kala masala.
Add water to form a gravy and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and simmer in the gravy for 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot with bhakri.
why_it_works: Fourth genuinely distinct regional egg curry identity in the database (alongside Kolhapuri, Bengali, and Vidarbha saoji), using Khandesh's specific kala masala
Budget-friendly protein carrying an intensely regional flavour
Deep, dark, bold spicing distinct from every other egg curry already used

name: ZITLAS Cluster Beans and Peanut Dinner Bowl
description: A dry, peanut-forward preparation of cluster beans (gavar) — a distinct dinner-portioned, richer version from the lighter breakfast Gavar Bhaji already in this collection.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric.
Add chopped gavar, cover and cook 10-12 minutes until tender, adding minimal water so it stays dry.
Stir in a generous amount of crushed peanuts.
Serve as a dry side with bhakri.
why_it_works: Higher peanut ratio and drier consistency than the bhakri-paired breakfast version already in this collection, giving more protein per serving for an evening meal
Same vegetable, deliberately different nutritional purpose and preparation style
Good textural contrast — dry and crunchy rather than saucy

name: ZITLAS Ash Gourd Chana Dal Dinner Bowl
description: Ash gourd cooked together with chana dal — a distinct vegetable-legume combination not resembling any other ash-gourd or chana dal recipe in the database.
instructions: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric.
Add ash gourd and soaked chana dal with water, and pressure cook for 2 whistles until both are tender.
Serve hot with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Combining ash gourd with chana dal in one pot is a genuinely different vegetable-legume pairing from any other ash-gourd dish or chana dal preparation already in the database
Chana dal adds meaningful protein and texture to an otherwise very light vegetable
One-pot, simple technique

name: ZITLAS Post-Workout Bhagar Khichdi Bowl
description: Proso millet (bhagar) cooked khichdi-style with moong dal, specifically timed for after an evening workout — a distinct grain choice from the rice-based post-workout amti bowls already in the database.
instructions: Rinse bhagar and moong dal together.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and turmeric, add the bhagar and moong dal with water (1:3 ratio).
Cover and simmer 12-15 minutes until soft.
Serve hot within 45-60 minutes of finishing an evening workout.
why_it_works: Bhagar's different amino acid and fiber profile from rice gives users a genuinely different post-workout carbohydrate source from the rice-based amti bowls already in the database
Easy to digest, well suited to eating soon after exercise
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Family-Style Khandeshi Vegetable Rassa
description: A vegetable-only version of the fiery Khandesh kala masala curry, scaled for family sharing — a distinct plant-based, family-portioned option within the Khandeshi flavour family introduced in this batch.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until deep golden, add garlic and kala masala.
Add the vegetables and water, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve family-style on a large platter with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Gives fully plant-based users and families access to Khandesh's distinctive fiery flavour, alongside the chicken and egg versions in this batch
Budget-friendly way to feed several people the same bold regional flavour
Scaled specifically for sharing

name: ZITLAS Leftover Bhakri Vegetable Casserole Bake
description: Leftover bhakri layered with vegetables and curd, then baked — a genuinely different leftover-rescue format from the crumbled upma or chivda uses of leftover bhakri already in the database.
ingredients: Leftover bhakri, torn into pieces — 150 g
instructions: Saute vegetables briefly with cumin seeds and turmeric.
Layer torn bhakri pieces and the sauteed vegetables in a small baking dish, pouring curd over each layer.
Bake at 190°C for 18-20 minutes until the top is lightly set and golden.
Serve warm, sliced like a casserole.
why_it_works: Layered casserole-bake format is a genuinely different leftover-rescue technique from the crumbled, pan-tossed upma or crisped chivda uses of leftover bhakri already in the database
Curd adds protein and moisture the dry bhakri lacks
Good way to use up several days' worth of leftover bhakri at once

name: ZITLAS Mixed Millet Dinner Khichdi
description: Bhagar, ragi and jowar combined in one khichdi — the most millet-diverse khichdi in the database, distinct from any single-millet or single-grain khichdi already used.
instructions: Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and turmeric.
Add bhagar, ragi flour and moong dal with water (roughly 1:3 ratio), stirring to prevent the ragi flour from clumping.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles until soft.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Combining three different millet/grain sources gives a broader fiber and mineral spread than any single-millet khichdi already in the database
Genuinely different grain composition from the rice-based or single-millet khichdis elsewhere
Naturally gluten-free, easy to digest

name: ZITLAS Roasted Kurdai Snack Bites
description: Dried rice-lentil kurdai roasted dry until crisp, eaten as a crunchy snack — distinct from the rehydrated, curried lunch use of kurdai already in this collection.
ingredients: Dried kurdai, broken into small pieces — 40 g
instructions: Heat oil, add the dried kurdai pieces directly and roast on low heat, stirring frequently, until crisp, about 6-8 minutes.

why_it_works: Dry-roasting rather than rehydrating gives a completely different crunchy snack texture from the curried Kurdai Bhaji already in this collection
Shelf-stable, portable
Quick to prepare

name: ZITLAS Baked Sandge Chips Snack
description: Dried sandge pieces baked until crisp — a distinct baked-chip format from the rehydrated, curried breakfast use of sandge already in this collection.

Cool before eating.
why_it_works: Baked chip format is a genuinely different way to eat sandge from the soft, curried breakfast bowl already in this collection
Very low added oil compared to a fried version
High protein, shelf-stable

name: ZITLAS Chikoo Peanut Chaat Snack
description: Chopped chikoo tossed with crushed peanuts and a squeeze of lime — a distinct sweet-savoury fruit chaat from any other fruit-based snack already in the database.

Toss with crushed peanuts and lemon juice.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Chikoo's natural caramel-like sweetness against peanuts and lime is a genuinely different fruit chaat combination from any other in the database

Fold into curd along with a pinch of black salt.

why_it_works: Ber's crisp, apple-like texture against curd is a genuinely different fruit-curd combination from the karvand, jambhul or grape versions already used in this collection

name: ZITLAS Amla Chutney Dip Snack
description: A thicker amla chutney served as a dip with raw vegetable sticks — a distinct application from the toast-spread use of amla chutney already in this collection.

Serve as a dip alongside cucumber and carrot sticks.

Vitamin-C-rich snack

description: Thin sev tossed dry with roasted peanuts and Khandeshi spicing — a distinct dry snack from the wet, gravy-based Shev Bhaji already used in this collection.

Toss with a pinch of kala masala.
Eat immediately while crisp.

Quick, minimal preparation
Portable, shelf-stable if made without moisture

name: ZITLAS Baked Gavar Chips Snack
description: Cluster beans sliced thin lengthwise and baked into crisp chips — a distinct vegetable-chip base from the karle or suran chips already in the database.

Toss with oil, turmeric and salt.
Arrange in a single layer on a tray and bake at 180°C for 16-18 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Cool before eating.
why_it_works: A third distinct vegetable-chip base for the database, alongside the karle and suran chips already used
Cluster beans' natural fibrous texture crisps well when baked thin
Very low calorie, high fiber

name: ZITLAS Roasted Ash Gourd Seeds Snack
description: Ash gourd seeds, cleaned and roasted, eaten as a crunchy snack — a genuinely unique seed source not used anywhere else in the database, made from what's usually a discarded part of the vegetable.

Toss with salt and red chilli powder.

name: ZITLAS Custard Apple Pulp Snack Cup
description: Fresh custard apple pulp eaten plain in a portable cup — the simplest, quickest way to enjoy sitaphal, distinct from the paneer-paired lunch bowl already in this collection.

name: ZITLAS Solapur Kardai Chutney Snack Bowl
description: A thicker version of the roasted safflower seed chutney, served as a standalone dip bowl with khakhra — a distinct serving format from the toast-spread breakfast version already in this collection.

Solapur regional specialty seed in a portable format

name: ZITLAS Khandesh Shev Bhaji Deluxe Special
description: A richer version of Khandeshi shev bhaji topped with a boiled egg and extra peanuts — a more indulgent 'special' variant distinct from the standard breakfast bowl already in this collection.

name: ZITLAS Kala Masala Special Curry Bowl
description: A vegetable-and-paneer curry built specifically to showcase Khandesh's signature kala masala blend as the star flavour — a distinct 'specials' entry celebrating the spice itself rather than a specific traditional dish.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until deep golden, add kala masala and vegetables, cooking 5 minutes.
Add water and paneer, simmering 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot with bhakri, letting the kala masala be the dominant flavour.
why_it_works: Specifically designed to let Khandesh's distinctive spice blend shine as the headline flavour, rather than being one ingredient among many — a genuine 'specials' concept celebrating the region's signature seasoning itself
Combines vegetables and paneer in one bowl, distinct from the single-protein Khandeshi dishes already in this batch
Rich, warming, intensely spiced

name: ZITLAS Nagpur Santra Barfi-Inspired Protein Bites
description: A ZITLAS adaptation of Nagpur's orange-flavoured barfi, made with milk powder and fresh orange zest instead of khoya — celebrating Nagpur's citrus identity in a protein-boosted sweet bite.
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai, add milk powder, orange zest and juice, and sugar or jaggery, stirring continuously.
Cook on low heat until it forms a thick, pliable dough, about 6-8 minutes.
Press into a flat tray, cool, and cut into small squares.
why_it_works: A ZITLAS adaptation using milk powder instead of the traditional khoya (reduced milk solids), giving notably more concentrated protein per bite
Specifically celebrates Nagpur's identity as India's 'Orange City', distinct from any other Nagpur recipe already in the database (which used dried orange peel in a chivda)
Fresh citrus zest gives a bright, distinct flavour from a plain milk sweet

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Wangi Zunka Combo Thali
description: A combination thali pairing Khandeshi-spiced eggplant bharit with a small portion of zunka and bhakri — a multi-component special distinct from either dish served alone elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Cook a bhakri as usual.
Roast and mash the eggplant with kala masala for the bharit.
Separately prepare a small portion of zunka with besan.
Plate the bharit, zunka and bhakri together as a combination thali.
why_it_works: Combining two distinct Khandeshi-region preparations into one considered thali, rather than serving either alone, is a genuinely different meal structure from any single-dish recipe already in the database
Showcases the breadth of Khandesh's kala-masala-based cooking in one meal
Traditional way Khandeshi thalis are actually composed

name: ZITLAS Solapur Kardai Oil Bhakri Special
description: A jowar bhakri cooked specifically with safflower (kardai) oil instead of the usual groundnut or refined oil — highlighting Solapur's distinctive traditional cooking-oil identity.
instructions: Knead jowar flour with warm water into a soft dough.
Pat out by hand into a thick round.
Cook on a hot tawa, brushing with safflower oil instead of the usual groundnut or refined oil, until browned on both sides.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Safflower oil is a traditional Solapur-region cooking oil with a distinct flavour from the groundnut or refined oils used elsewhere in the database, made from the same kardai seeds already introduced in this collection
Highlights a genuinely different regional cooking-fat tradition, not just a different flour or filling
Simple, single-ingredient-change 'special' that still represents authentic regional practice

name: ZITLAS Sitaphal Protein Bowl
description: Custard apple pulp blended with Greek yogurt — a protein-boosted dessert bowl celebrating Marathwada's sitaphal, distinct from the plain lunch pairing already in this collection.
instructions: Deseed the custard apple.
Blend or mash the pulp with Greek yogurt and cardamom powder.
Chill and serve as a dessert bowl.
why_it_works: Greek yogurt gives this notably more protein than the plain pulp or the savoury paneer-paired lunch version already in this collection
Naturally creamy and sweet, needs no added sugar
Distinct dessert-bowl format from the plain snack cup already used

name: ZITLAS Amla Murabba-Inspired Protein Bites
description: A ZITLAS adaptation of amla murabba (candied gooseberry preserve), made into portion-controlled no-cook bites bound with nuts instead of a heavy sugar syrup.
instructions: Blend amla with dates into a sticky paste.
Mix in crushed almonds until well combined.
Shape into 8 small bites.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving; store refrigerated for up to a week.
why_it_works: Traditional murabba is heavily sugar-preserved; this adaptation uses dates and nuts instead, giving a genuinely lighter, no-added-sugar version while keeping amla as the star ingredient
Portable, portion-controlled bites rather than a syrupy preserve eaten by the spoonful
Vitamin-C-rich fruit in a genuinely different format from the chutney uses already in this collection

name: ZITLAS Ber Halwa Bowl
description: A portion-controlled halwa made from cooked, mashed ber (jujube) — a distinct fruit-based halwa from the vegetable-based (lauki, gajar) halwas already in the database.
instructions: Simmer deseeded ber with milk for 10-12 minutes until very soft.
Mash and continue cooking with ghee and jaggery for 3-4 minutes until it thickens into a halwa consistency.
Serve warm in a small bowl.
why_it_works: Ber as the base gives a genuinely different fruit-forward halwa from the vegetable-based lauki or gajar halwas already in the database
Single-serving, portion-controlled format
Uses a widely available, low-cost seasonal fruit

name: ZITLAS Kohla Halwa Protein Bowl
description: A portion-controlled halwa made from ash gourd with a spoon of milk powder for extra protein — a distinct vegetable-based dessert from the lauki, gajar or ber halwas already in the database.
instructions: Squeeze excess water from the grated ash gourd.
Heat ghee, add the ash gourd and saute 5 minutes.
Add milk and simmer until reduced, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in milk powder and jaggery, cooking 2-3 more minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Ash gourd's very high water content makes this a genuinely lower-calorie halwa base than the denser lauki or gajar versions already in the database
Milk powder addition gives more protein than a traditional version
Fourth distinct vegetable-based halwa in the collection, each with real textural differences

name: ZITLAS Chikoo Protein Shake Bowl
description: A thick, spoonable chikoo shake blended with milk and a little Greek yogurt — a distinct dessert-bowl format from the plain curd bowl use of chikoo already in this collection.
instructions: Blend chikoo, milk and Greek yogurt together until thick and smooth (use less liquid than a drinkable shake).
Pour into a bowl — thick enough to eat with a spoon.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: Thick, spoonable bowl format with Greek yogurt gives more protein and a different eating experience from the plain curd bowl already using chikoo in this collection
Chikoo's natural caramel sweetness needs no added sugar
Distinct dessert format from the drink version

name: ZITLAS Amla Shot Drink
description: A concentrated amla-and-honey shot — a distinct small-format wellness drink from the chutney or bite uses of amla already in this collection.
instructions: Blend amla with a little water until smooth.
Strain to extract just the juice.
Stir in honey.
Drink as a small, concentrated shot, not a full glass.
why_it_works: Concentrated shot format is a genuinely different way to consume amla from the chutney or nut-bound bites already used in this collection
Traditionally taken this way for its vitamin C content
Very small serving, distinct from a diluted drink

name: ZITLAS Chikoo Milkshake Drink
description: A classic chikoo milkshake, blended smooth and drinkable — distinct from the thick spoonable dessert bowl version already in this collection by being a genuine sipping drink.
instructions: Blend chikoo, milk and cardamom powder until smooth and pourable.
Chill and serve in a glass.
why_it_works: Thin, drinkable consistency is genuinely different from the thick, spoon-eaten dessert bowl already using chikoo in this collection
Naturally sweet, no added sugar needed
Classic Maharashtrian milkshake format

name: ZITLAS Kokum Amla Cooler
description: A fusion cooler combining kokum and amla — two distinct Maharashtrian souring fruits blended into one drink, offering a genuinely layered tartness not found in either fruit alone.
instructions: Soak kokum in a little warm water.
Blend the kokum water with amla, remaining water and jaggery until smooth.
Strain if a smoother drink is preferred.
Chill and serve.
why_it_works: Combining two distinct souring fruits (kokum's fruity tang and amla's sharper vitamin-C tartness) into one drink gives a genuinely layered flavour not found in either alone
Both fruits are traditionally used for cooling and digestive purposes
Distinct from the pure solkadhi or pure amla drinks already used separately

name: ZITLAS Khandeshi Buttermilk Jeera Drink
description: A spiced buttermilk with a touch of Khandeshi kala masala instead of the usual plain roasted cumin — a distinct regional twist on chaas.
instructions: Whisk curd with water until smooth.
Stir in a small pinch of kala masala and black salt.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: Kala masala addition gives a distinctly different, spicier profile from the plain roasted-cumin Curd Chaas Jeera Drink already in the database
Small pinch keeps it a refreshing drink rather than a spicy dish
Regional flavour twist on an everyday preparation

name: ZITLAS Sitaphal Milkshake Drink
description: A drinkable custard apple milkshake — distinct from the thick, spoonable dessert bowl or plain snack cup uses of sitaphal already in this collection.
instructions: Deseed the custard apple.
Blend the pulp with milk and cardamom powder until smooth and pourable.
Chill and serve in a glass.
why_it_works: Thin, drinkable format is the third distinct use of sitaphal in this collection, alongside the protein bowl and plain snack cup
Naturally very sweet, needs no added sugar
Classic Maharashtrian seasonal milkshake

name: ZITLAS Ber Sherbet Drink
description: A diluted, drinkable ber sherbet — distinct from the curd bowl or halwa uses of ber already used elsewhere in this collection.
instructions: Simmer deseeded ber with jaggery and a little water for 5 minutes until softened.
Mash and strain to extract the juice.
Dilute with the remaining water and chill.
Serve cold.
why_it_works: Diluted sherbet format is a third distinct use of ber in this collection, alongside the curd bowl snack and halwa dessert
Naturally sweet-tart, refreshing
Very low cost, widely available fruit
